title: Align agents --check with the bridge selected by init --codex
summary: Align agents --check with the bridge selected by init --codex
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

In a fresh disposable Git repository with Quest initialized:
  lore init --yes --tracker quest --codex
  lore agents --check --json
Observed: exit 6; the check proposes creating .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md while the selected Codex bridge is unchanged. Installing both bridges makes the check pass. Orbitfall likewise needed lore agents to add the Claude bridge before a clean check.
Expected: check the selected/installed bridge set by default, or provide an explicit documented bridge scope so a valid Codex-only setup can pass its drift check. LCLI-281 (Done) implemented independent bridge selection at init; this follow-up concerns the consistency of its resulting check contract.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fresh supported Codex-only initialization has a documented drift-check command that exits 0 without requiring another bridge.
Check scope and defaults are explicit in help/instructions.
Regression coverage includes Codex-only, Claude-only, both bridges and actual selected-bridge drift.

implementationNotes:
Investigated before assuming any code change was needed. The CONCRETE bug this task reports (a Codex-only lore init --codex repository's lore agents --check proposing an uninvited Claude bridge and never passing its own gate) was already fixed by LCLI-442 (PR #568, hasClaudeBridge symmetric to the existing hasCodexBridge), whose own final summary explicitly says "Fixed the concrete bug behind LCLI-437." Reproduced live against current dev to confirm rather than trust the cross-reference: lore init --yes --tracker none --codex then lore agents --check --json now exits 0, reporting only the two Codex-shaped files (.codex/skills/lore/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md) as unchanged, no Claude bridge proposed. AC1 was already satisfied.

Remaining real gaps, verified directly against the current source and test suite rather than assumed:
AC2 ("Check scope and defaults are explicit in help/instructions") was genuinely unmet -- lore agents --help's manifest entry is a deliberately terse one-line summary by this codebase's own design (core/manifest.ts: "so an agent learns the whole CLI surface in one read instead of parsing prose"), so the presence-based Codex/Claude scoping logic lived only in source comments, invisible to a user or agent who doesn't read agents.ts. Added a new `lore instructions agents` topic (core/instructions.ts, mirroring the existing check/sync/linking/validation/workspace topics' style and depth) explaining: which bridge a bare `lore agents` covers and why (presence-based, Codex opt-in via lore init --codex, Claude default-on except when Codex-alone is selected); that an explicit `lore init --claude/--agents/--codex` always means exactly what it asks regardless of what else exists; and how `[agents] skill_source = "plugin"` interacts with the bare-call scoping. New test asserting the topic's key content, plus added to the existing topic-resolution table test.

AC3 ("Regression coverage includes Codex-only, Claude-only, both bridges and actual selected-bridge drift") was mostly already covered by LCLI-442's own test suite (test/agents.test.ts): a dedicated LCLI-437 describe block already covers Codex-only check/write, the fresh-repo Claude default, an explicit scoped Claude request on a Codex-only repo, and both-bridges-selected; a separate LCLI-364 describe block covers Claude-only and BOTH-artifact drift detection (AGENTS.md and .codex SKILL.md). The one genuine gap, found by reading every existing drift test's own fixture setup rather than assuming coverage from the test names alone: every drift test in the LCLI-364 block calls agents() (creating the Claude bridge) THEN withCodexBridge() -- none of them ever prove drift detection works on a repository that ONLY ever selected Codex, the exact LCLI-437 shape. Added that missing test: a Codex-only-selected repo whose own codex SKILL.md drifts still fails the gate at exit 6 and names the file, with no uninvited Claude bridge reported alongside it.

Full suite 2886 pass (5 new: 1 in agents.test.ts, 1 new + 1 extended in instructions.test.ts, plus the topic-list extension), 1 skip (pre-existing), 0 fail. typecheck clean; lint exit 0 (one pre-existing unrelated warning); lore check 77 files, 0 errors. No opum-cli-e2e row needed -- this is entirely lore-internal behavior/documentation, not a cross-CLI contract.
